statements.disagree: Rescuing key banks and firms with public money is sometimes necessary.
statements.note: About rescuing failing businesses.

statements.text: A liberal democracy's courts and institutions should not constrain what a national majority has chosen.
statements.agree: Once a national majority has decided, courts and independent bodies should not block it.
statements.disagree: Courts and independent institutions should be able to overrule the majority to protect rights and rules.
statements.note: About majority will versus judicial checks.

statements.text: Public bodies should be required to have equal or near-equal representation of women and men.
statements.agree: Quotas or rules make sure women and men are about equally represented in public bodies.
statements.disagree: Public bodies should be filled on merit or by voters, without gender quotas.
statements.note: About gender quotas in public bodies.

statements.text: A country and its colonies should form a self-sufficient economic bloc shut off from outside trade.
statements.agree: A nation should aim to produce what it needs and limit dependence on foreign trade.
statements.disagree: Countries gain from open trade and should not wall themselves off.
statements.note: About economic self-sufficiency versus open trade.

statements.text: International trade agreements should include binding labor and environmental standards.
statements.agree: Trade deals should require workers' rights and environmental protections, with penalties.
statements.disagree: Trade deals should stick to trade, leaving labor and environment to each country.
statements.note: About conditions attached to trade agreements.

statements.text: Material incentives should be replaced as the main spur to work by moral incentives and a sense of social duty.
statements.agree: People should work mainly out of social duty and shared purpose, not personal pay.
statements.disagree: Pay and personal reward are the best way to motivate work.
statements.note: About what should motivate work.

statements.text: A small armed group can create the conditions for revolution rather than waiting for them to appear.
statements.agree: A determined armed vanguard can spark a wider uprising.
statements.disagree: Revolution needs conditions and mass support to mature first.
statements.note: About starting revolutions versus waiting for them.

statements.text: Hereditary titles and privileges should be abolished.
statements.agree: Nobody should hold rank or privilege by birth.
statements.disagree: Hereditary titles and ranks are a legitimate part of a country's order.
statements.note: About inherited rank and privilege.

statements.text: School history should be taught with the student's own nation or civilization at its centre.
statements.agree: History lessons tell the story mainly through the students' own nation or civilization.
statements.disagree: History lessons give every region and civilization equal weight, with none at the centre.
statements.note: About whose story history lessons put first.

statements.text: More advanced societies may rightly rule less advanced ones for a time in order to bring them improvement.
statements.agree: Temporary rule by a more developed society can be justified if it helps the ruled to progress.
statements.disagree: No society may rule another, whatever the stated aim.
statements.note: About rule over other peoples for their supposed benefit.

statements.text: Schools should teach pupils loyalty and pride toward the nation, its flag and its anthem.
statements.agree: Public schools should build patriotic feeling and respect for national symbols.
statements.disagree: Schools should teach about the nation without promoting loyalty or pride.
statements.note: About patriotism as a goal of schooling.

statements.text: Racial preferences in college admissions and hiring should be abolished.
statements.agree: Applicants should be judged without regard to race, even to help disadvantaged groups.
statements.disagree: Race may be taken into account to widen opportunity for underrepresented groups.
statements.note: About race-conscious admissions and hiring.

statements.text: New money should be created by a public body rather than by private banks lending.
statements.agree: The state, not commercial banks, should decide how much new money enters the economy.
statements.disagree: Banks creating money as they lend is acceptable, under central bank or market discipline.
statements.note: About who should create money.

statements.text: Capitalism can adapt to its crises and avoid a general collapse.
statements.agree: Credit, regulation and growth let capitalism survive its downturns indefinitely.
statements.disagree: Its contradictions will eventually bring it down in a general crisis.
statements.note: About whether capitalism is bound to collapse.

statements.text: A country should cultivate political and cultural influence in regions once ruled by its predecessor empire.
statements.agree: A state may reasonably build ties and influence across lands its imperial predecessor once ruled.
statements.disagree: Past imperial rule gives a country no special claim to influence in those regions.
statements.note: About influence in a former empire's territories.

statements.text: Poor countries should break their economic ties with rich countries rather than seek integration into the world market.
statements.agree: Developing countries should cut dependence on rich-world trade and capital.
statements.disagree: Developing countries do best by joining the world economy.
statements.note: About delinking poor countries from the world market.

statements.text: Workers in rich countries are mostly not exploited, and share in the profits that rich countries extract from poor ones.
statements.agree: Rich-country workers benefit from global inequality and are not the exploited class.
statements.disagree: Workers everywhere are exploited and share the same basic interests.
statements.note: About whether rich-country workers are exploited.

statements.text: Private owners should be free to refuse to associate with, hire or serve anyone on any grounds, even where this means discrimination.
statements.agree: Property owners decide whom they deal with, and anti-discrimination law violates that freedom.
statements.disagree: Businesses open to the public must not discriminate, and the law may require it.
statements.note: About freedom of association versus anti-discrimination law.

statements.text: A written bill of rights that ordinary majorities cannot easily amend should limit what government may do.
statements.agree: Basic rights should be written down and shielded from passing majorities.
statements.disagree: Rights should be left to legislatures and ordinary law, which can change them.
statements.note: About entrenched written guarantees of rights.

statements.text: Colonial-era treaties that divided a people without consulting it have no binding force today.
statements.agree: Borders and treaties imposed by colonial powers without local consent can be set aside.
statements.disagree: Inherited borders and treaties stand, however they were first drawn.
statements.note: About whether colonial borders keep their legitimacy.

statements.text: Rulers should be chosen by election among the political nation rather than inherit the throne.
statements.agree: The head of state is picked by an electorate, not born into the role.
statements.disagree: Inheritance can legitimately decide who rules.
statements.note: About election versus inheritance for the top office.

statements.text: A decision should not bind a dissenting minority, even a single member, without its consent.
statements.agree: No majority may impose a rule on those who refuse it, and one member can block a law.
statements.disagree: Majorities may decide for everyone, and the minority must comply.
statements.note: About majority rule versus the consent of each member.

statements.text: Subjects may lawfully resist or remove a ruler who breaks the constitutional laws and the trust placed in him.
statements.agree: A ruler who breaks the law forfeits obedience and can be removed.
statements.disagree: Subjects owe obedience even to a ruler who breaks the law.
statements.note: About a right to resist unlawful rulers.

statements.text: Parliament, not the monarch, should be the supreme lawmaking authority.
statements.agree: The elected assembly has the last word on law, above the crown or executive.
statements.disagree: The monarch or executive holds the final say, or courts can overrule parliament.
statements.note: About where final lawmaking power lies.

statements.text: Animals are sentient beings whose suffering matters morally.
statements.agree: Animals can suffer, and that suffering counts in how we treat them.
statements.disagree: Animals have no moral standing, or only what humans give them.
statements.note: About the moral weight of animal suffering.

statements.text: Animals may be kept and used for food or research, provided their suffering is kept to a minimum.
statements.agree: Using animals is acceptable if they are treated humanely.
statements.disagree: Using animals is wrong however well they are treated, or needs no limits.
statements.note: About human use of animals.

statements.text: The wealthy and privileged have a duty to look after those less fortunate than themselves.
statements.agree: Wealth and rank bring obligations toward the poor.
statements.disagree: Wealth carries no special duty beyond respecting others' rights.
statements.note: About duties that come with privilege.

statements.text: A good life is best lived withdrawn from public affairs rather than taking part in politics.
statements.agree: A quiet private life is better than political engagement.
statements.disagree: Taking part in public life is part of a good life or a duty.
statements.note: About whether a good life includes politics.

statements.text: Mass culture and the media serve to pacify people and reproduce the existing social order.
statements.agree: Entertainment and media keep people passive and tied to the system as it is.
statements.disagree: Mass culture and media are mostly entertainment, information or free expression, not tools of social control.
statements.note: About how culture and media shape politics.

statements.text: The ruling class maintains power mainly by winning the consent of the governed through culture and institutions, not only by force.
statements.agree: Elites rule largely because people accept their ideas and institutions as natural.
statements.disagree: Power rests mainly on force, law or the real interests and choices of the governed.
statements.note: About how power is kept without constant force.

statements.text: Poor countries stay poor because the world economy is structured to transfer their surplus to richer countries.
statements.agree: Trade, finance and investment drain wealth from poorer nations to richer ones.
statements.disagree: Poor countries stay poor mainly because of their own policies, institutions or circumstances.
statements.note: About why some countries are poor.

statements.text: Public offices should be reserved for native-born citizens.
statements.agree: Only people born in the country should hold public office.
statements.disagree: Naturalized citizens should be able to hold any public office.
statements.note: About whether citizens by birth and by naturalization are equal.

statements.text: Each country's communist or socialist party should choose its own road to socialism without direction from another country's party.
statements.agree: Parties follow their own national conditions and answer to no foreign party.
statements.disagree: Parties of different countries should follow a common line set by a leading party.
statements.note: About national independence within an international movement.

statements.text: A poor country should rely on its own resources for development rather than on foreign aid, loans or investment.
statements.agree: Development should be paid for at home, even if it is slower, to stay independent.
statements.disagree: Foreign aid, loans and investment are a sound way to speed up development.
statements.note: About independence versus outside help in development.

statements.text: A country should demand the return of territory it lost to a neighbour in a past war.
statements.agree: Land lost in an old war can rightly be claimed back.
statements.disagree: Borders settled by past wars should be accepted rather than reopened.
statements.note: About reopening old border settlements.

statements.text: The descendants of a country's pre-colonial peoples should hold political leadership over the descendants of settlers.
statements.agree: Political leadership should belong to the country's original peoples.
statements.disagree: Leadership should be open to all citizens whatever their ancestry.
statements.note: About ancestry and who should lead.

statements.text: Anti-fascism should be regarded as a founding value of a democratic constitution.
statements.agree: A democratic constitution should rest on rejecting fascism.
statements.disagree: Anti-fascism is one stance among others, not a founding value of the constitution.
statements.note: About the foundations of a democratic state.

statements.text: Fascism and communism should be condemned together as equivalent forms of totalitarianism.
statements.agree: Both are the same kind of evil and deserve the same condemnation.
statements.disagree: The two differ in aims and record and should not be put on one level.
statements.note: About comparing fascism and communism.

statements.text: Slavery was not the main cause of the American Civil War.
statements.agree: States' rights, tariffs and other disputes drove the war more than slavery did.
statements.disagree: Slavery was the main cause of the war and of secession.
statements.note: About the causes of the American Civil War.

statements.text: Public monuments and flags honoring figures from a country's past should be preserved even when those figures are now widely condemned.
statements.agree: Old monuments stay as part of the nation's heritage.
statements.disagree: Monuments to widely condemned figures should be removed or moved.
statements.note: About what to do with monuments to controversial history.

statements.text: Boys and men facing disadvantage in education, health and suicide deserve the same public attention and programmes as girls and women.
statements.agree: Problems that fall mainly on males deserve public programmes of their own.
statements.disagree: Public programmes should go where the need is greatest, which is not mainly with boys and men.
statements.note: About public attention to men's problems.

statements.text: Domestic violence by women against men is as serious as violence by men against women and should receive equal services and protection.
statements.agree: Abused men need the same shelters, services and protection as abused women.
statements.disagree: Domestic violence falls mostly on women and services should reflect that.
statements.note: About domestic violence and gender.

statements.text: Western political institutions do not suit every civilization, which may develop its own forms of government.
statements.agree: Each civilization can build political forms from its own values.
statements.disagree: Democratic and liberal institutions suit every society.
statements.note: About whether one political model fits all.

statements.text: The armed forces should play a political role as guardians of order and the constitution.
statements.agree: The military may step in to protect order and the constitution.
statements.disagree: The military should stay out of politics and obey elected civilians.
statements.note: About the army's role in politics.

statements.text: Unpaid domestic and care work should be recognised and paid as labour.
statements.agree: Housework and care at home count as work and deserve wages.
statements.disagree: Housework and care are family duties, not work to be paid by others.
statements.note: About the value of unpaid work at home.

statements.text: Adult children owe their parents lifelong respect, care and support.
statements.agree: Grown children are bound to honour and look after their parents for life.
statements.disagree: Adult children's obligations to parents are a matter of personal choice and affection.
statements.note: About duties between generations in a family.

statements.text: Government posts should be filled by competitive examination of learning and ability rather than by election or patronage.
statements.agree: Officials are chosen by tested merit, not by votes, birth or connections.
statements.disagree: Public office should go to those chosen by voters or by those they appoint, not by examination.
statements.note: About how rulers and officials are selected.

statements.text: Governments should block foreign companies from buying firms in strategic industries.
statements.agree: The state can stop foreign buyers from taking over key national businesses.
statements.disagree: Firms should be free to be sold to any buyer, foreign or domestic.
statements.note: About foreign ownership of important industries.

statements.text: Adults should be free to end a marriage without having to prove fault.
statements.agree: Either spouse can leave a marriage without showing wrongdoing by the other.
statements.disagree: Ending a marriage should require grounds such as fault, or be made hard by law.
statements.note: About how easily marriages can be dissolved.

statements.text: Elected leaders should be bound by the decisions of those who chose them and be removable at any time.
statements.agree: Representatives act as delegates who can be instructed and recalled whenever the community decides.
statements.disagree: Representatives use their own judgment and serve a fixed term unless removed by regular process.
statements.note: About how tightly representatives answer to voters.

statements.text: Pensions should be paid from individual savings accounts managed by private companies rather than from a state pay-as-you-go system.
statements.agree: Each worker saves for their own retirement in a private account.
statements.disagree: Pensions are paid by the state from current taxes or contributions shared among all workers.
statements.note: About who provides retirement income.

statements.text: Land should belong to the community or the nation, with individuals holding it only for as long as they use it.
statements.agree: Land is held in common and people keep it only while they work or live on it.
statements.disagree: Individuals should be able to own land outright and keep, sell or leave it idle.
statements.note: About whether land can be owned privately.

statements.text: A government should need an elected parliament's approval of its budget before it may spend.
statements.agree: The elected legislature must approve spending before the government can use public money.
statements.disagree: The government may raise and spend money without legislative approval.
statements.note: About who controls the public purse.

statements.text: One language should be the sole common language of the state, schooling and public life, even where this restricts the use of other languages.
statements.agree: The state makes one language the common medium of government, schooling and commerce.
statements.disagree: Several languages keep equal standing in public life and schooling.
statements.note: About whether one language should be imposed as the common public language.

statements.text: Foreigners should not be allowed to own land in the country.
statements.agree: Land stays in the hands of citizens; foreigners may not buy it.
statements.disagree: Foreigners may buy and own land on the same terms as citizens.
statements.note: About foreign ownership of land.

statements.text: A policy that produces unequal outcomes between racial groups should be treated as discriminatory, whatever its intent.
statements.agree: Unequal outcomes show discrimination, and such policies should be reviewed or repealed.
statements.disagree: Discrimination means intentional unequal treatment, not unequal outcomes.
statements.note: About whether discrimination is judged by intent or by effect.

statements.text: The pursuit of ever more possessions and status goods does more harm than good to people and society.
statements.agree: Consumerism breeds waste, status competition and unhappiness; people should consume less.
statements.disagree: Consumer demand and the enjoyment of possessions are good for people and society.
statements.note: About whether a consumer culture is harmful.

statements.text: My country should arm and fund insurgents fighting governments it considers hostile.
statements.agree: Supporting foreign armed movements is a legitimate way to weaken hostile governments.
statements.disagree: A country should not arm or fund rebels in other countries.
statements.note: About supporting foreign insurgencies.

statements.text: A great power may send troops into an allied country without its government's consent to stop it leaving the alliance or abandoning its political system.
statements.agree: The bloc's leader may intervene to keep its members in line.
statements.disagree: Allied countries decide their own alliances and systems, and no ally may intervene by force.
statements.note: About military intervention within an alliance or bloc.

statements.text: Corporations have too much influence over government through lobbying and campaign money.
statements.agree: Business money and lobbying shape laws and politicians more than voters do.
statements.disagree: Business lobbying and donations are a normal part of politics and do not decide outcomes.
statements.note: About the weight of corporate money in politics.

statements.text: Governments should be able to restrict foreign funding of NGOs, media and universities to protect national sovereignty.
statements.agree: The state may limit or screen money that foreign donors give to civil society, press and schools.
statements.disagree: Civil society, media and universities may take funding from abroad without state restriction.
statements.note: About foreign money in domestic politics and civil society.

statements.text: The state should give families financial incentives to have more children, rather than rely on immigration to offset population decline.
statements.agree: Tax breaks and payments for parents are the right answer to a falling birth rate.
statements.disagree: Birth rates are a private matter, and immigration or other measures can handle population decline.
statements.note: About how the state should respond to falling birth rates.

statements.text: Local authorities should be able to limit purchases of homes and land in their area to people who live there.
statements.agree: An area may keep homes and land for its own residents, shutting out second-home and outside buyers.
statements.disagree: Anyone may buy homes and land anywhere, wherever they live.
statements.note: About restricting property purchases by non-residents.

statements.text: Governments should guarantee a job to everyone willing to work, acting as employer of last resort.
statements.agree: The state offers public work to anyone who wants a job and cannot find one.
statements.disagree: Jobs come from the private market, and the state should not promise work to all.
statements.note: About whether the state should guarantee employment.

statements.text: Democracies rarely go to war with one another, so spreading democracy makes the world more peaceful.
statements.agree: More democracies means fewer wars, so promoting democracy serves peace.
statements.disagree: Regime type does little to prevent war, and spreading democracy does not bring peace.
statements.note: About whether democracy promotes peace between states.

statements.text: People have no general moral duty to obey the law merely because it is the law.
statements.agree: A law binds only when it is just or you choose to follow it, not simply because it was passed.
statements.disagree: Citizens owe obedience to the law as such, even to laws they dislike.
statements.note: About whether being law creates a duty to obey.

statements.text: No state or group of states has the right to intervene in the internal affairs of another, for any reason.
statements.agree: Outside powers may never interfere in another country's internal affairs, whatever the reason.
statements.disagree: Outside powers may sometimes interfere in another country's affairs, for example to stop atrocities.
statements.note: About whether states may intervene in each other's internal affairs.

statements.text: Workers should be organized in unions by industry rather than by craft.
statements.agree: All workers in an industry belong in one union, whatever their trade.
statements.disagree: Workers are better organized by craft or trade, or in unions of their own choosing.
statements.note: About how workers should organize into unions.

statements.text: A particular ethnic or religious minority is secretly conspiring against the nation.
statements.agree: A hidden minority plots against the nation and its people.
statements.disagree: Claims that a minority secretly conspires against the nation are false.
statements.note: About conspiracy claims against minorities.

statements.text: Marriage should not be a legal institution that confers state benefits and property rights.
statements.agree: The state should not recognize marriage or attach special benefits and rights to it.
statements.disagree: Legal marriage with its benefits and rights is a worthwhile institution.
statements.note: About whether the state should recognize marriage.

statements.text: Everyone should have a legal right of access to government information.
statements.agree: Citizens may demand government records, and secrecy needs a strong justification.
statements.disagree: Governments may keep their records and deliberations confidential as they see fit.
statements.note: About public access to government records.

statements.text: Food and goods should mainly be produced and bought close to where they are consumed.
statements.agree: Local production and buying local should be the norm, with long supply chains the exception.
statements.disagree: Goods should be made wherever it is most efficient, however far they travel.
statements.note: About local versus distant production and trade.

statements.text: Political struggle should be organized in small informal groups of people who trust one another, rather than in permanent parties, unions or federations.
statements.agree: Small, informal, trust-based groups are the right form for political action.
statements.disagree: Lasting formal organizations such as parties and unions are needed for political action.
statements.note: About how political movements should organize.

statements.text: A country's own constitution and courts should take precedence over international law and international courts.
statements.agree: National law and courts have the last word, whatever treaties or international courts say.
statements.disagree: International law and courts can rightly override a country's own laws.
statements.note: About national versus international legal authority.

statements.text: The national community should be defined by a shared religion.
statements.agree: Belonging to the nation goes with sharing its religion.
statements.disagree: Nationality does not depend on religion, and people of any faith belong equally.
statements.note: About whether religion defines the nation.

statements.text: Foreign states should show deference to a leading power through ritual submission and tribute in return for recognition and trade.
statements.agree: Weaker states should acknowledge a leading power's primacy through ritual and tribute.
statements.disagree: States should deal with one another as formal equals, without ritual submission.
statements.note: About whether states should defer to a leading power.

statements.text: Revenue raised in a region should mostly be spent in that region rather than shared with other regions.
statements.agree: A region should keep most of the money it raises rather than subsidize others.
statements.disagree: Revenue should be pooled and shared across regions according to need.
statements.note: About whether regions should keep the revenue they raise.

statements.text: Personal belongings should remain private while the means of production are held in common.
statements.agree: Ordinary personal possessions stay private, but factories, land and tools belong to everyone.
statements.disagree: Either all property should be private, or common ownership should extend to personal belongings too.
statements.note: About the line between personal possessions and productive property.

statements.text: Communism should be defeated rather than coexisted with.
statements.agree: Communism is a threat to be defeated, not a rival system to live alongside.
statements.disagree: Communist states can be coexisted with and should not be targeted for defeat.
statements.note: About whether to coexist with or defeat communism.

statements.text: Public services should be delivered by a mix of public, private and independent providers within a publicly funded system.
statements.agree: Publicly funded services can be run by private and independent providers as well as the state.
statements.disagree: Publicly funded services should be run directly by the state, not by private providers.
statements.note: About who should deliver publicly funded services.

statements.text: Religion is an illusion that consoles people for real suffering and will fade once their material conditions improve.
statements.agree: Religious belief mainly answers hardship and loss, and fades as life gets better and fairer.
statements.disagree: Religion answers lasting human needs and will endure whatever people's material conditions.
statements.note: About why people are religious and whether religion will last.

statements.text: Capitalism has been a historically progressive force that created the material basis for a better society.
statements.agree: Capitalism built the productive power and wealth that later and better societies rest on.
statements.disagree: Capitalism has been mainly a harmful or regressive stage, not a foundation for something better.
statements.note: About how to judge capitalism over the long run.

statements.text: Women's equality cannot be fully achieved without transforming the economic system.
statements.agree: Women's subordination is tied to how the economy is organised, so reform of laws and attitudes is not enough.
statements.disagree: Women's equality can be reached within the existing economic system through law and changing attitudes.
statements.note: About whether economic change is needed for gender equality.

statements.text: Housework and childcare should be provided as public services rather than done privately within families.
statements.agree: Cooking, cleaning and child care should be shared through public kitchens, nurseries and similar services.
statements.disagree: Housework and child care are best left to families and private arrangements.
statements.note: About who should carry out domestic and care work.

statements.text: Words borrowed from foreign languages should be purged from the national language.
statements.agree: Foreign loanwords should be replaced by native words, by official policy if needed.
statements.disagree: Borrowed words are a normal part of a living language and need no purging.
statements.note: About keeping a national language free of foreign words.

statements.text: Treaties between a government and a nation within its borders should remain binding until both parties agree to change them.
statements.agree: Such treaties are lasting promises that the government cannot cancel or rewrite on its own.
statements.disagree: A government may change or end such treaties when it judges the public interest requires it.
statements.note: About whether treaties with internal nations can be overridden.

statements.text: Society should be reorganised into small self-governing cooperative communities that hold their property in common.
statements.agree: People should live and work in communities that own land and goods together and govern themselves.
statements.disagree: Society should stay organised around nation-states, markets and private or state property.
statements.note: About communal living as a model for society.

statements.text: The majority ethnic group should be encouraged to settle in regions where minorities are the majority.
statements.agree: The state should promote settlement of the majority group in minority regions to bind them to the nation.
statements.disagree: The state should not steer majority settlement into regions where minorities are the majority.
statements.note: About state-promoted settlement in minority regions.

statements.text: Neither capitalism nor communism offers a sound basis for society; a third course is needed.
statements.agree: Both capitalism and communism fail, and society should follow a different, third way.
statements.disagree: One of the two, capitalism or communism, is the sound basis, or other options are not needed.
statements.note: About whether a third way exists between capitalism and communism.

statements.text: A people's historical or religious tie to a land gives it a stronger claim than the claims of other peoples now living there.
statements.agree: A long historical or religious bond to a land outweighs the claims of those who live there now.
statements.disagree: Present residents' claims count at least as much as another people's ancient or religious tie to the land.
statements.note: About whether historical or religious ties to land outweigh the claims of current inhabitants.

statements.text: The Holocaust did not happen as historians describe it.
statements.agree: The mass murder of Europe's Jews by Nazi Germany was invented or greatly exaggerated.
statements.disagree: The Holocaust happened as historians describe it.
statements.note: About whether the established historical account of the Holocaust is accurate.

statements.text: Sexual relations between adults of the same sex should be a criminal offence.
statements.agree: Same-sex relations between consenting adults should be punishable by law.
statements.disagree: The law should not punish consenting adults for same-sex relations.
statements.note: About criminal penalties for same-sex relations.

statements.text: Political opposition and independent organisations should be suppressed to preserve order.
statements.agree: The state should shut down opposition parties and independent groups when they threaten order.
statements.disagree: Opposition and independent organisations should be free to operate, even when they challenge those in power.
statements.note: About whether the state may suppress opposition and independent groups.

statements.text: The civil government may punish public blasphemy and the open practice of false religion.
statements.agree: The state may punish public mockery of the true faith and open practice of other religions.
statements.disagree: The state should not punish blasphemy or the public practice of any religion.
statements.note: About legal penalties for blasphemy and for practising other religions.

statements.text: A country's overseas territories should be governed for the economic benefit of the ruling country.
statements.agree: Colonies should be run mainly to supply markets, materials and outlets for the ruling country.
statements.disagree: Overseas territories should not be run for the economic benefit of the ruling country.
statements.note: About whose interests colonial rule should serve.

statements.text: When non-Muslim forces invade a Muslim land, armed resistance becomes an obligation on every Muslim.
statements.agree: Every Muslim has a duty to join the armed defence of an invaded Muslim land.
statements.disagree: Armed defence of an invaded land is a matter for its own people and state, not a duty on all believers.
statements.note: About whether armed defence of invaded Muslim lands is a duty on all Muslims.

statements.text: Rulers who do not govern by religious law may be declared illegitimate and removed by force.
statements.agree: A ruler who sets aside religious law forfeits legitimacy and may be overthrown by arms.
statements.disagree: A ruler's legitimacy does not depend on governing by religious law, and force against rulers on that ground is wrong.
statements.note: About armed removal of rulers who do not apply religious law.

statements.text: Ordinary people should take part directly in the decisions that shape their lives, in workplaces, communities and universities, rather than leaving them to distant officials.
statements.agree: Citizens should have a direct say in decisions where they work, live and study.
statements.disagree: Decisions are best left to elected officials and professional managers.
statements.note: About direct participation in everyday decisions.

statements.text: Racism, sexism and class oppression overlap and cannot be addressed one at a time.
statements.agree: Different forms of oppression compound each other and must be tackled together.
statements.disagree: Racism, sexism and class inequality are separate problems that can be addressed separately.
statements.note: About whether forms of oppression must be tackled together.

statements.text: Transgender people should be legally recognised and protected according to their gender identity.
statements.agree: The law should treat transgender people as the gender they identify with, including in gender-based protections.
statements.disagree: The law should recognise sex as assigned at birth for legal and protected categories.
statements.note: About legal recognition of gender identity.

statements.text: Medical professionals should be allowed to help terminally ill adults end their lives.
statements.agree: Terminally ill adults should be able to get medical help to die.
statements.disagree: Doctors should not be allowed to help anyone end their life.
statements.note: About assisted dying for terminally ill adults.

statements.text: The division of politics into left and right is outdated, and the best ideas of each should be combined.
statements.agree: Left and right are obsolete labels; good policy draws on both.
statements.disagree: Left and right still describe real, lasting differences in politics.
statements.note: About whether the left-right divide still makes sense.

statements.text: Work under capitalism alienates people from their own creative activity.
statements.agree: Wage work cuts people off from the meaning and creativity of what they make.
statements.disagree: Wage work is ordinary employment, and alienation is not a special feature of capitalism.
statements.note: About whether market labor stunts human self-realisation.

statements.text: Islam is incompatible with the culture and values of Western countries.
statements.agree: Islam clashes with Western culture and values at a basic level.
statements.disagree: Islam and Western culture and values can coexist.
statements.note: About whether Islam can fit Western societies.

statements.text: Political authority ultimately comes from God rather than from the people.
statements.agree: Rulers hold their authority from God and answer to divine law, not to popular sovereignty.
statements.disagree: Authority comes from the people, who delegate it to those who govern.
statements.note: About where political authority comes from.

statements.text: Public officials and state-school students should not wear religious dress in state institutions.
statements.agree: State institutions stay free of visible religious dress for staff and pupils.
statements.disagree: People may wear religious dress in state institutions as they do elsewhere.
statements.note: About religious symbols in public institutions.

statements.text: Employers should not be able to use nondisclosure agreements or mandatory arbitration to keep sexual harassment complaints out of court.
statements.agree: Harassment complaints must be able to reach court and be made public, whatever workers signed.
statements.disagree: Employers and workers may agree to confidential settlements and arbitration as a matter of contract.
statements.note: About limits on private contracts that silence harassment claims.

statements.text: A market economy should be combined with social protection and fair competition rules, rather than left to laissez-faire or run by the state.
statements.agree: Markets work best inside rules that protect competition and guarantee social security.
statements.disagree: Markets are best left free of such rules, or the state should run the economy.
statements.note: About the middle course between free markets and state control.

statements.text: Countries should abolish their armed forces.
statements.agree: A country can and should do without a standing military.
statements.disagree: A country needs armed forces to defend itself.
statements.note: About whether states should keep militaries at all.

statements.text: Some people and regions may be allowed to grow rich first so that others can follow step by step.
statements.agree: Uneven early growth is acceptable if it leads to general prosperity later.
statements.disagree: Prosperity should be shared evenly from the start, without some being left behind.
statements.note: About accepting uneven development on the way to prosperity.

statements.text: My country should stay out of the military blocs of rival great powers.
statements.agree: A country stays neutral and non-aligned rather than joining either bloc.
statements.disagree: A country is safer and more useful as a member of an alliance or bloc.
statements.note: About neutrality versus joining great-power blocs.

statements.text: The leader of a state may be succeeded in office by his or her child.
statements.agree: Supreme office can pass within one family from parent to child.
statements.disagree: Supreme office should be filled by election or merit, never inherited.
statements.note: About inheritance of political power.

statements.text: Credit should be issued at cost by banks owned by their users rather than by profit-making banks.
statements.agree: Loans come from user-owned mutual banks that charge only what running them costs.
statements.disagree: Banks may lend for profit and charge interest, or the state should run credit.
statements.note: About who should supply credit and at what price.

statements.text: Governments should refuse austerity conditions imposed by international lenders such as the IMF.
statements.agree: A country should reject spending cuts demanded in return for loans and set its own course.
statements.disagree: Lenders may rightly require spending cuts and reforms in return for loans.
statements.note: About who sets economic policy when a country owes money abroad.

statements.text: The right to vote should be limited to those who own property or pay a minimum amount of tax.
statements.agree: Only people with a stake in the country, shown by property or taxes paid, should vote.
statements.disagree: Every adult citizen should vote regardless of wealth.
statements.note: About whether wealth should decide who may vote.

statements.text: The domination of women and the domination of nature are connected and should be ended together.
statements.agree: Exploiting nature and subordinating women stem from the same logic of domination, and each struggle needs the other.
statements.disagree: The oppression of women and the exploitation of nature are separate problems with separate causes.
statements.note: About whether the subordination of women and of nature are linked.

statements.text: Under capitalism, relations between people take the form of relations between things, so that economic forces seem to rule human beings.
statements.agree: Markets make social relations look like natural laws of things, hiding that people made them and could change them.
statements.disagree: Markets are a neutral way of coordinating people and do not distort how we see social relations.
statements.note: About whether market society disguises human relations as relations between things.

statements.text: Freedom of the press and of assembly mean little while the rich own the presses and the meeting halls.
statements.agree: Formal press and assembly rights are hollow when wealth decides who can actually be heard.
statements.disagree: Press and assembly freedoms are real and valuable even where media and venues are privately owned.
statements.note: About whether formal freedoms depend on who owns the media.

statements.text: Rulers should govern only through publicly announced standing laws applied by known judges, not by decrees made case by case.
statements.agree: Government must act under fixed, published laws that apply alike to all and are enforced by regular courts.
statements.disagree: Rulers may act by decree or discretion when circumstances or the public good require it.
statements.note: About whether rulers are bound by fixed, published law.

statements.text: The right to vote and hold office should be limited to members of one racial or ethnic group.
statements.agree: Only members of the nation's dominant racial or ethnic group should take part in government.
statements.disagree: Voting and office-holding should not depend on race or ethnicity.
statements.note: About whether race or ethnicity should decide who may vote.

statements.text: Citizens should be able to take part in political deliberation and decisions over the internet.
statements.agree: Online platforms should let ordinary people debate and decide public questions directly.
statements.disagree: Political deliberation and decisions belong in physical meetings, elections and legislatures.
statements.note: About using the internet for political participation.

statements.text: Government decision-making records and citizen proposals should be published openly so the public can trace how each was handled.
statements.agree: The public should be able to see and download how decisions were made and how proposals were treated.
statements.disagree: Governments may keep decision-making records closed where openness is costly or unhelpful.
statements.note: About public access to the records of government decisions.

statements.text: The law should restrict marriage between members of different religions.
statements.agree: The state may limit or scrutinise marriages across religious lines to protect a community.
statements.disagree: Adults may marry across religions without legal restriction.
statements.note: About whether law should limit marriage across religions.

statements.text: Consumers should deliberately avoid shops owned by members of a particular religious minority.
statements.agree: Members of the majority religion should buy only from their own and shun a minority's businesses.
statements.disagree: Shoppers should not single out businesses by the religion of their owners.
statements.note: About boycotting businesses by owners' religion.

statements.text: Randomly selected groups of citizens should be convened to deliberate on, and help decide, major public questions.
statements.agree: Ordinary people chosen by lot should study and weigh big issues, and their conclusions should count.
statements.disagree: Major public questions are best decided by elected representatives, experts and referendums.
statements.note: About using chosen-by-lot citizens' assemblies in decision-making.

statements.text: Religious law and doctrine should be reinterpreted for modern conditions rather than followed as medieval authorities fixed them.
statements.agree: Believers should rethink inherited rulings in light of reason and today's circumstances.
statements.disagree: The rulings and doctrines handed down by the classical authorities should be kept as they are.
statements.note: About updating religious teaching versus preserving it.

statements.text: Great concentrations of wealth endanger a free society.
statements.agree: Very rich citizens can dominate politics and bend the law, so liberty needs a rough equality of means.
statements.disagree: Large fortunes are compatible with a free society and need not be curbed to protect liberty.
statements.note: About whether wealth inequality threatens political freedom.

statements.text: Gay and lesbian people should be allowed to serve openly in the armed forces.
statements.agree: Sexual orientation should not bar anyone from military service or force them to hide it.
statements.disagree: Open service by gay and lesbian people harms military order, or the ban or concealment should stay.
statements.note: About open LGB service in the military.

statements.text: The state should actively promote atheism through its schools and public education.
statements.agree: Public education should teach that religion is false and encourage unbelief.
statements.disagree: The state should stay neutral on religious belief or support it, not promote unbelief.
statements.note: About state promotion of unbelief.

statements.text: Police and prisons should be abolished and replaced with other ways of providing safety.
statements.agree: Safety should come from community care, mediation and social provision rather than policing and incarceration.
statements.disagree: Police and prisons are needed to keep people safe and should be kept, even if reformed.
statements.note: About whether policing and prison should exist at all.

statements.text: In a deeply divided society, major communities should share executive power rather than be governed by simple majority rule.
statements.agree: Each main community should have a guaranteed place in government, even against a numerical majority.
statements.disagree: Government should follow the majority, with no guaranteed shares for particular communities.
statements.note: About power-sharing versus majority rule where communities are deeply split.

statements.text: Private charities and local communities help the poor better than government programs do.
statements.agree: Churches, charities and neighbours know people and get results; the state should leave more of this to them.
statements.disagree: Government programs reach more people and are more reliable than charity and community help.
statements.note: About who is best placed to help people in poverty.

statements.text: Elected politicians should be limited to a small number of terms in any office.
statements.agree: Term limits keep politics from becoming a career and bring in fresh people.
statements.disagree: Voters should be free to re-elect anyone, and experience in office is valuable.
statements.note: About limiting how long one person can hold elected office.

statements.text: Citizens should be able to delegate their vote on each policy area to someone they trust and withdraw that delegation at any time.
statements.agree: People can hand their vote on a topic to a trusted person and take it back whenever they like.
statements.disagree: Each citizen should vote for themselves, or leave decisions to elected representatives.
statements.note: About delegable, revocable voting as a form of democracy.

statements.text: Reducing the risk of human extinction should be a top priority of public policy.
statements.agree: Preventing catastrophes that could end humanity deserves major, well-funded attention.
statements.disagree: Present problems should come first; extinction risks are too speculative to be a top priority.
statements.note: About how much weight long-term catastrophic risks get against present needs.

statements.text: Women should be eligible for every leadership and teaching office in religious institutions on the same terms as men.
statements.agree: Women may be clergy, preachers and teachers like men.
statements.disagree: Some religious offices are rightly reserved for men.
statements.note: About women's access to religious office.

statements.text: Authority within a marriage should be shared between the spouses rather than held by the husband.
statements.agree: Spouses decide together as equals.
statements.disagree: The husband is the head of the household and has final authority.
statements.note: About authority between spouses in a marriage.

statements.text: Foreign residents should be allowed to vote in local elections.
statements.agree: Long-term residents without citizenship have a say in the places where they live.
statements.disagree: Voting is reserved for citizens at every level.
statements.note: About who counts as part of the local electorate.

statements.text: Rents should be capped by law in areas of housing shortage.
statements.agree: The law limits how much landlords can charge where homes are scarce.
statements.disagree: Rents are set by the market, with supply as the remedy.
statements.note: About whether the state should set housing prices.

statements.text: Patents and copyrights should be abolished.
statements.agree: Ideas and creative works can be copied freely; no one holds a legal monopoly on them.
statements.disagree: Inventors and creators keep legal rights over their work for a time.
statements.note: About whether intellectual property is legitimate property.

statements.text: Young people should be organised into uniformed, drilled youth movements that train them for national service.
statements.agree: Youth belong to disciplined organisations that prepare them to serve the nation.
statements.disagree: Young people's associations should be free, voluntary and not run for national ends.
statements.note: About whether the state or movement should organise youth.

statements.text: Nuclear weapons should not be based on my country's territory.
statements.agree: No nuclear weapons, ours or an ally's, should be stationed here.
statements.disagree: Hosting nuclear weapons can be part of keeping the country safe.
statements.note: About where nuclear weapons may be kept.

statements.text: A country should not host foreign military bases on its territory.
statements.agree: Foreign armies should leave; hosting them compromises sovereignty.
statements.disagree: Hosting allied bases can be a fair price for security and investment.
statements.note: About foreign troops on national soil.

statements.text: Governments should formally recognise past mass killings of a people as genocide.
statements.agree: States should officially name and acknowledge such killings.
statements.disagree: Such labels are for historians and courts, not for official government recognition.
statements.note: About official recognition of historical atrocities.

statements.text: Income should reward useful work, not merely the ownership of property.
statements.agree: Rents, interest and returns on idle wealth are unearned and should give way to pay for useful work.
statements.disagree: Owning and investing property is itself a productive contribution and earns a legitimate return.
statements.note: About whether ownership alone justifies income.

statements.text: It is wrong to kill another person even in self-defence or in defence of others.
statements.agree: Taking a life is never justified, even to stop an attacker.
statements.disagree: Lethal force is sometimes a legitimate last resort to protect oneself or others.
statements.note: About whether killing can ever be justified.

statements.text: A nation's identity runs in unbroken continuity from its ancient origins to the present.
statements.agree: Today's nation is the same people as its ancient and medieval forebears.
statements.disagree: National identities are recent and changing, not continuous from antiquity.
statements.note: About how old and continuous nations are.

statements.text: Sex, and not only gender, is socially constructed.
statements.agree: Even the categories of male and female are shaped by culture and language.
statements.disagree: Sex is a biological fact; only gender roles are cultural.
statements.note: About whether biological sex is fixed or socially shaped.

statements.text: Feminist politics should not be founded on a single, fixed category of 'women'.
statements.agree: Women differ too much for one shared identity to anchor a political movement.
statements.disagree: Women share common interests and a common identity that politics can rest on.
statements.note: About whether 'women' is a stable political group.

statements.text: Those who die for the nation should be honoured as martyrs and saints.
statements.agree: Sacrificial death for the nation deserves sacred public veneration.
statements.disagree: Honouring the national dead should stay secular and restrained.
statements.note: About how far the nation's dead are made sacred.

statements.text: Politics is fundamentally a spiritual struggle between good and evil.
statements.agree: Public life is at bottom a fight between spiritual forces, not only interests.
statements.disagree: Politics is about interests, institutions and compromise, not cosmic struggle.
statements.note: About whether politics is a moral or spiritual war.

statements.text: A national homeland should serve as a cultural and spiritual centre for a diaspora rather than gather all of its people.
statements.agree: The homeland inspires a people living elsewhere without needing to hold them all.
statements.disagree: A homeland should be where the whole people lives.
statements.note: About what a homeland is for.

statements.text: Cultural renewal of a nation should come before building its state.
statements.agree: A people must revive its culture first; a state built earlier would be hollow.
statements.disagree: A state comes first and creates the conditions for national culture.
statements.note: About whether culture or the state comes first.

statements.text: God should not be described in exclusively male terms.
statements.agree: Religious language and imagery should include more than male terms for God.
statements.disagree: Traditional male language for God should be kept as it is.
statements.note: About how religion speaks of God.

statements.text: Religious texts and traditions should be judged by whether they promote the full humanity of women.
statements.agree: Teachings that diminish women should be set aside as not authoritative.
statements.disagree: Religious texts are authoritative as they stand, not subject to such a test.
statements.note: About the standard for judging religious tradition.

statements.text: A country's economic life should be in the hands of members of the national majority rather than of minority groups.
statements.agree: Trade and business should mainly be run by the national majority.
statements.disagree: Economic roles should be open to all regardless of group.
statements.note: About whether economic life should be tied to nationality.

statements.text: Administrative regions where one people live should be merged into a single territorial unit for that people.
statements.agree: A people should have one region of its own rather than being split across several.
statements.disagree: Regional borders need not follow where a people live.
statements.note: About whether internal borders should follow peoples.

statements.text: Trade unions should be independent of the state and of any ruling party.
statements.agree: Unions answer to their members, not to the government or a party.
statements.disagree: Unions may be run or guided by the state or a ruling party.
statements.note: About whether unions should stand apart from the state.

statements.text: A society cannot be called socialist unless the working class itself holds real political power.
statements.agree: Without workers' own political power, state ownership is not socialism.
statements.disagree: State ownership of the economy is enough to make a society socialist, whoever rules.
statements.note: About what counts as socialism.

statements.text: Local essentials such as water, hospitals and local transport should remain in public hands.
statements.agree: Basic local services stay publicly owned and run.
statements.disagree: Local services can be sold or contracted to private companies.
statements.note: About keeping basic local services public.

statements.text: A legislature should include a second chamber alongside the directly elected parliament.
statements.agree: A second chamber adds a further check on the elected parliament.
statements.disagree: One directly elected chamber is enough.
statements.note: About whether lawmaking needs two chambers.

statements.text: The means of production should be owned by the local community, neither by private owners nor by the national state.
statements.agree: Farms, factories and utilities belong to the town or city that uses them.
statements.disagree: Productive property belongs to private owners or to the national state.
statements.note: About who should own the economy's main assets.

statements.text: Towns and cities should join in confederations whose delegates coordinate and administer but do not govern, leaving decisions with local assemblies.
statements.agree: Local assemblies decide, and joint councils only carry out and coordinate.
statements.disagree: Joint bodies may make binding decisions over the towns that join them.
statements.note: About how far local communities should hand power upward.

statements.text: A worker's wage should be enough to support the worker and his family.
statements.agree: Pay should cover a household, not only the individual worker.
statements.disagree: Pay should reflect the work done, whatever the worker's family needs.
statements.note: About whether wages should cover a family.

statements.text: Regulators should approve new drugs and medical devices faster.
statements.agree: Treatments should reach patients sooner, accepting more risk.
statements.disagree: Long, careful testing before approval should be kept.
statements.note: About speed against caution in medical approval.

statements.text: Governments should fund dramatically expanded research into slowing or reversing ageing.
statements.agree: Public money should go into extending healthy life.
statements.disagree: Ageing is natural and research money is better spent elsewhere.
statements.note: About public funding for anti-ageing research.

statements.text: People should be able to send and receive money without the government being able to trace or block it.
statements.agree: Payments can be private and beyond state control.
statements.disagree: The state should be able to trace and stop payments.
statements.note: About financial privacy against the state.

statements.text: People should be free to take part online anonymously or under pseudonyms without having to reveal their legal identity.
statements.agree: Anyone can speak and act online without giving their real name.
statements.disagree: People online should be identifiable by their legal identity.
statements.note: About anonymity online.

statements.text: The state exists to serve the person, and no person may be treated merely as a means to the ends of the community or the state.
statements.agree: Each person has a worth the state and community may not override.
statements.disagree: The community or state may sometimes use individuals for its larger ends.
statements.note: About the worth of the person against the collective.

statements.text: Human beings have a spiritual as well as a material nature, and politics should serve both.
statements.agree: People need meaning and spirit, not only material goods.
statements.disagree: Human needs are essentially material and politics should deal with those.
statements.note: About whether politics should serve spiritual needs.

statements.text: A region's self-government should rest on powers that the national legislature can reduce or withdraw.
statements.agree: The national parliament stays the final authority and can take powers back.
statements.disagree: Regional powers are protected and cannot be taken away by the national parliament.
statements.note: About whether regional powers are entrenched.

statements.text: Genetically engineered crops should be embraced as a tool for sustainable agriculture.
statements.agree: Gene-edited crops can feed people with less land and chemicals.
statements.disagree: Genetically engineered crops should be avoided or strictly limited.
statements.note: About genetically engineered crops.

statements.text: Dense cities are better for the environment than suburbs and the countryside.
statements.agree: Compact city living uses less energy and land per person.
statements.disagree: Lower-density living is as good or better for the environment.
statements.note: About city density and the environment.

statements.text: Racial groups have distinct political interests, and members of each should organise to defend them.
statements.agree: People of a race may organise politically as a group.
statements.disagree: Politics should not be organised along racial lines.
statements.note: About organising politically by race.

statements.text: Pride in one's own race or ancestry is legitimate and should not be treated as shameful.
statements.agree: Taking pride in one's race or ancestry is fine.
statements.disagree: Racial pride is a harmful attitude.
statements.note: About pride in race or ancestry.

statements.text: Armed forces should be used only to defend the country against attack, never to start wars.
statements.agree: Force is for self-defence alone.
statements.disagree: Force may also be used to pursue a country's aims abroad.
statements.note: About when a country may use force.

statements.text: A people who share a language and history form one nation, whatever state borders or religions divide them.
statements.agree: Shared language and history make a nation.
statements.disagree: A shared language alone does not make one nation.
statements.note: About whether language defines a nation.

statements.text: Members of each religious community should vote for their own representatives in separate electorates.
statements.agree: Each community should elect its own representatives.
statements.disagree: All citizens should vote in common electorates.
statements.note: About separate electorates for religious communities.

statements.text: Foreign powers are plotting to partition and weaken my country.
statements.agree: Outside powers are working to break up and weaken the country.
statements.disagree: Claims of foreign plots to break up the country are exaggerated.
statements.note: About foreign plots against the country.

statements.text: Public colleges and universities should be free of tuition.
statements.agree: Public higher education should charge no tuition.
statements.disagree: Students should pay tuition at public colleges.
statements.note: About tuition at public colleges.

statements.text: Pollution and the use of finite resources should be taxed so that polluters pay, rather than relying mainly on regulation or subsidies.
statements.agree: Putting a price on pollution and resource use is the main way to protect the environment.
statements.disagree: Regulation, public investment or other tools should do more than taxes to protect the environment.
statements.note: About taxing pollution versus other environmental tools.

statements.text: Present generations owe it to future generations to hand on the Earth undamaged.
statements.agree: We have a duty to leave the planet in good condition for those who come after us.
statements.disagree: We owe little to people not yet born, or may use resources as we judge best.
statements.note: About duties to future generations.

statements.text: Women tend to bring distinct values, such as care, cooperation and nonviolence, to public life, and these should be given more weight.
statements.agree: Women's typical outlook adds something different to politics that deserves more weight.
statements.disagree: Women and men bring the same range of values, or gender should not shape how views are weighed.
statements.note: About whether women bring distinct values to public life.

statements.text: Armaments should be reduced to the lowest level consistent with national safety.
statements.agree: Countries should cut their weapons stockpiles and forces to the minimum needed for security.
statements.disagree: Countries should keep or build up arms as they see fit for their security.
statements.note: About reducing armaments by agreement.

statements.text: Treaties and diplomacy between governments should be conducted openly, with no secret international agreements.
statements.agree: International agreements should be negotiated and made in public view.
statements.disagree: Governments need confidential negotiations and some secret agreements.
statements.note: About openness in diplomacy.

statements.text: The state should control the movement of capital in and out of the country.
statements.agree: Governments should limit how money and investment can be moved across borders.
statements.disagree: Money and investment should be free to cross borders.
statements.note: About controls on cross-border capital flows.

statements.text: Only the state's army and police should be allowed to bear arms; all other armed groups should be disarmed.
statements.agree: Armed militias and private armies are disbanded; only state forces keep weapons.
statements.disagree: Other armed groups, such as militias or resistance forces, may legitimately keep their weapons.
statements.note: About who may hold armed force inside a country.

statements.text: Soldiers should refuse orders to fight in wars between states.
statements.agree: Individual soldiers and conscripts have a duty to refuse to fight in state wars.
statements.disagree: Soldiers should obey lawful orders, including orders to fight in their country's wars.
statements.note: About whether conscience should override military orders.

statements.text: Wages and working conditions should be set by collective bargaining between unions and employers rather than by individual contracts.
statements.agree: Workers bargain as a group through unions, producing common rules for a whole workplace or industry.
statements.disagree: Each worker and employer should agree terms individually.
statements.note: About how pay and conditions should be negotiated.

statements.text: Governments should top up the incomes of low-paid working families through tax credits.
statements.agree: The state adds to the pay of low-income working households through the tax system.
statements.disagree: Pay should be left to employers and the market, or low incomes helped by other means.
statements.note: About supplementing low wages with public money.

statements.text: Governments should be bound by legal fiscal rules that limit how much they can borrow.
statements.agree: Borrowing limits written into law stop governments from running up debt.
statements.disagree: Governments should decide borrowing case by case, without fixed legal limits.
statements.note: About rules that restrain public borrowing.

statements.text: The rules of the international economy should be restructured in favour of developing countries.
statements.agree: Trade, finance and debt rules should be changed to give poorer countries a fairer share.
statements.disagree: The existing international economic rules are broadly fair and should be kept.
statements.note: About reforming the global economic order.

statements.text: The existing state machinery should be smashed and replaced, not taken over and used.
statements.agree: A revolution should dismantle the old bureaucracy, army and courts and build new organs of power.
statements.disagree: The existing state can be taken over or reformed and used for new purposes.
statements.note: About whether to use or destroy the existing state.

statements.text: Different communities should be free to try different economic systems, with no fixed blueprint for the economy of a free society.
statements.agree: Markets, sharing and cooperatives can coexist, and communities choose their own arrangements.
statements.disagree: A free society needs one agreed economic system, set out in advance.
statements.note: About pluralism over how an economy should be organised.

statements.text: Ecosystems and natural resources should be counted as capital whose value is reflected in the economy.
statements.agree: Nature should be priced and accounted for like other assets, so its depletion shows up as a cost.
statements.disagree: Nature's worth cannot or should not be expressed in economic terms.
statements.note: About putting an economic value on nature.

statements.text: The nation is a sacred community that outlasts its individual members and gives their lives lasting meaning.
statements.agree: The nation is a sacred, enduring community in which individuals find lasting meaning.
statements.disagree: The nation is a practical political arrangement, not a sacred one.
statements.note: About whether the nation is treated as sacred.

statements.text: Governments should cancel or relieve the student loan debts of graduates.
statements.agree: Public action should wipe out or reduce what graduates owe on student loans.
statements.disagree: Borrowers should repay the student loans they chose to take on.
statements.note: About relieving student loan debt.

statements.text: A wealthy central region of a state can exploit its poorer regions much as a colonial power exploits colonies.
statements.agree: Rich core regions can subordinate and drain poorer ones inside the same country.
statements.disagree: Regional inequality within a state is not exploitation of the kind colonies suffered.
statements.note: About whether regional inequality is a form of colonial exploitation.

statements.text: There is a shared human nature that grounds human dignity and rights and should not be redesigned.
statements.agree: A common human nature underlies dignity and rights, and tampering with it is wrong.
statements.disagree: Human nature is not fixed or sacred, and dignity does not depend on it.
statements.note: About whether human nature is a fixed basis for dignity.

statements.text: Governments should fund independent public service media that are free of government and commercial control.
statements.agree: Publicly funded broadcasters, kept independent, should be part of the news system.
statements.disagree: News should be left to private outlets and the market, not funded by the state.
statements.note: About publicly funded independent media.

statements.text: All authentic religions express one underlying spiritual truth.
statements.agree: Behind their different forms, the great religions point to one shared truth.
statements.disagree: Religions make rival claims, and at most one of them can be right.
statements.note: About whether the world's religions share one truth.

statements.text: The state should protect farmers from market swings and moneylenders through guaranteed crop prices, public purchase or cooperative credit.
statements.agree: Farmers get price floors, state buying or cheap cooperative credit to keep them secure.
statements.disagree: Farm prices and credit are left to the market, without state guarantees.
statements.note: About state support for farmers.

statements.text: A country should keep its nuclear weapons rather than disarm unilaterally while rival powers hold theirs.
statements.agree: Giving up nuclear arms alone would be unsafe, so a country keeps them until others disarm too.
statements.disagree: A country should give up its nuclear weapons even if others keep theirs.
statements.note: About unilateral nuclear disarmament.

statements.text: Working people should have their own political party, independent of the established parties.
statements.agree: Workers need a party of their own to represent their interests in government.
statements.disagree: Working people are best represented within broad parties that cover all classes.
statements.note: About independent parties for working people.

statements.text: Female genital mutilation should be prohibited by law.
statements.agree: The law should ban cutting of girls' and women's genitals, whatever the custom.
statements.disagree: This is a matter of custom and community, not for criminal law.
statements.note: About legal bans on female genital cutting.

statements.text: Women should have the same legal right as men to inherit and own land.
statements.agree: Daughters and widows inherit and own land on the same terms as sons and husbands.
statements.disagree: Inheritance and land follow custom or religious rules that may favour men.
statements.note: About equal inheritance and land rights for women.

statements.text: A language spoken in several regions is one language, whatever name each region gives it.
statements.agree: Varieties spoken across regions are one language, even if each region names it differently.
statements.disagree: Each region's variety can be its own language, and its name should be respected.
statements.note: About whether regional names make separate languages.

statements.text: Polluters should be legally liable to compensate or stop for any proven physical harm to other people's property, rather than being regulated by agencies.
statements.agree: Pollution is settled through lawsuits and injunctions by those harmed, not by agency rules.
statements.disagree: Agencies should set and enforce pollution rules in advance rather than leaving it to private suits.
statements.note: About courts versus regulators for pollution.

statements.text: Customary chiefs should have an official advisory role in making national law.
statements.agree: Traditional leaders sit in a recognised body that is consulted on laws touching custom.
statements.disagree: Lawmaking belongs to elected representatives alone, with no formal place for traditional leaders.
statements.note: About a formal role for traditional chiefs in lawmaking.

statements.text: Protecting the environment should take priority over individual liberty when the two conflict.
statements.agree: Where freedoms damage the environment, they should give way.
statements.disagree: Individual liberty should not be sacrificed to environmental goals.
statements.note: About trading freedom against environmental protection.

statements.text: Sentences for serious repeat offenders should be fixed by law rather than left to judges' discretion.
statements.agree: Mandatory sentences, such as three strikes, apply whatever a judge might prefer.
statements.disagree: Judges should weigh each case and set the sentence themselves.
statements.note: About fixed sentences versus judicial discretion.

statements.text: Immigrants should be required to learn the national language.
statements.agree: Learning the language is a duty of settling, and the state may require it.
statements.disagree: Learning the language is encouraged but should not be required of immigrants.
statements.note: About language requirements for immigrants.

statements.text: Workers should not be required to join or pay a union as a condition of employment.
statements.agree: Union membership and dues are voluntary, and no one can be required to pay them to hold a job.
statements.disagree: Where a union represents a workplace, all workers it covers can be required to join or pay their share.
statements.note: About compulsory versus voluntary union membership.

statements.text: Voters should have to show proof of citizenship and identification to vote.
statements.agree: Showing ID and proof of citizenship is a reasonable condition of voting, to protect the integrity of elections.
statements.disagree: Such requirements keep eligible people from voting and should not be imposed.
statements.note: About identification requirements at the ballot box.

statements.text: No single interpretation of a religion should have legal precedence over others in the state.
statements.agree: The state should treat all streams and interpretations of a religion equally under the law.
statements.disagree: The state may give one interpretation official status or authority over the others.
statements.note: About legal standing for different interpretations of a religion.

statements.text: A government is democratic if its rulers are chosen and removed in free and fair competitive elections, whatever policies it pursues.
statements.agree: Democracy is a method for choosing and removing rulers, and fair elections are enough to make a government democratic.
statements.disagree: Democracy also requires substance, such as real popular rule, rights or equality, beyond holding elections.
statements.note: About what makes a government democratic.

statements.text: Sex before or outside marriage is acceptable for women.
statements.agree: Women may have sexual relationships outside marriage without moral or social censure.
statements.disagree: Sex belongs within marriage, and women should not have it outside it.
statements.note: About sexual morality and marriage.

statements.text: Governments may cut internet access in a region or the whole country to maintain order.
statements.agree: Shutting down the internet is a legitimate tool in a crisis or unrest.
statements.disagree: Governments should never cut off internet access.
statements.note: About internet shutdowns.

statements.text: Welfare programs should be replaced by a cash payment that shrinks as a person's earnings rise.
statements.agree: One cash payment, withdrawn gradually as income grows, should replace separate welfare programs.
statements.disagree: Separate targeted welfare programs should be kept rather than folded into one cash payment.
statements.note: About a negative income tax versus existing welfare programs.

statements.text: Women should have the same right as men to vote and hold public office.
statements.agree: Women vote and stand for office on the same terms as men.
statements.disagree: Voting and office-holding may be limited to men or reserved for some groups.
statements.note: About women's political rights.

statements.text: Religion is a major cause of women's oppression.
statements.agree: Religious teaching and institutions are a main reason women have been held down.
statements.disagree: Religion is not a main cause of women's oppression, and often supports women.
statements.note: About religion's role in women's status.

statements.text: Racial categories are social constructs without a scientific basis.
statements.agree: Races are categories people invented and enforced, not natural divisions.
statements.disagree: Races are real biological groupings with meaningful natural differences.
statements.note: About whether race is a social or biological category.

statements.text: Governments should set up dedicated agencies, such as ministries or ombuds, to promote gender equality.
statements.agree: The state should have its own bodies charged with advancing gender equality.
statements.disagree: Gender equality should not need dedicated state agencies.
statements.note: About state machinery for gender equality.
